literal: Good than those who know, base people fortune they possess; in the heart sorrow they are without.
translation: The base are more fortunate than those who know what is good, for they have no sorrow in their hearts.
modern: நன்மை எது என்று அறிந்து செயல்படுபவர்களை விட கயவர்கள் பாக்கியசாலிகள்; ஏனென்றால் அவர்கள் மனதில் எந்தக் கவலையும் இருப்பதில்லை.
explanation: This couplet uses sharp irony to describe the nature of base people. It claims that the mean-spirited are luckier than the wise who know what is good. While good people constantly worry about doing the right thing and feel sorrow for the suffering of others, the base have no such moral anxiety. Because they lack a conscience, their hearts are completely free from distress.
